background.text: That was Senator Clinton's position during the campaign. The president didn't agree with it at that time. The president was right the first time. Here's how I know this stuff. We've done almost everything in the bill, and the truth is, in Vermont, 16 years ago when we did all this, we did it much better than what's in the bill now. And one of the things we did in the bill was eliminate the ability of insurance companies to turn anyone down for any reason other than nonpayment of premium. And we let them charge 20% more than their cheapest patient, which the Senate lets them charge three times as much as their cheapest patient. And we've had this system in place for 16 years. There's no mandate. It's true that we still have an uninsured rate of about 9.5%, which is actually low compared to most states. But we also have a vibrant insurance market, and so it really doesn't hurt the insurance market. So from kind of an intellectual point of view, you'd like a mandate, but you don't have to have one. You have to make the system work. And the mandate is not popular with anybody, because no American would like to be told what to do by the government.
